title: Collapsing nested power means
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $p>0$, and let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$. For $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, define $g(x)$ to be the uniform power mean of the two values $f(x,b)$ as $b$ ranges over $\{0,1\}$. Then the uniform power mean of $f$ on $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ equals the uniform power mean of $g$ on $\{0,1\}^n$.
replaced: Let $p>0$ and $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$, and write $M_{p,z}$ for the uniform power mean $(\E_z|\cdot|^p)^{1/p}$. Then $M_{p,(x,b)}f(x,b)=M_{p,x}\bigl(M_{p,b}f(x,b)\bigr)$, where $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ and $b\in\{0,1\}$.
